newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end limit down, new lows set.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end limit down, new lows set.

text.p: Active fund selling pushed CME lumber futures down for limit losses of $10.00 in July and September, and most months posted new contract lows, as cash indications continue to point lower, traders said.
Lumber closed $10.00 to $4.00 lower, with July limit down at $357.10 per tbf and September limit off at $354.00 per tbf. All but July and distant May posted new contract lows.
The market became technically weak as declining cash prices again weighed on the market. Fund selling added to pressure to touch off stop loss orders, they said.
Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $358 per tbf, down $4 from midweek and $6 under last Friday's level. This is the lowest price level since July 19, 1996, Random Lenghts said.

High prices encouraged stepped up production while demand has been no better than last year. Even with the recent break in cash markets the price is still high enough to keep production at a high leveli, cash sources said.
"These are still historically high (cash) prices," which prompted the large pace of production, said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

Further losses are seen Monday following the limit break and 100 unfilled sell orders in July. Also, July options traded synthetically $5.00 lower at $352.10. ABN Chicogo Corp notably sold July while Refco sold September. ING spread long September/short July, pit sources added.
